name: Sahara
hook: The world's largest hot desert, from Timbuktu's caravans to Saint-Exupéry's crash.

facts.label: largest hot desert
facts.statement: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert, covering more than 3 million square miles of North Africa.

facts.label: the Atlas Mountains
facts.statement: The Atlas Mountains separate the Mediterranean coast from the Sahara across Morocco and Algeria.

facts.label: Algeria and Libya
facts.statement: The Sahara covers about 85 percent of Algeria and 90 percent of Libya.

facts.label: Timbuktu
facts.statement: Timbuktu, a caravan city on the Sahara's southern edge in Mali, grew rich on trade and drew Mansa Musa's mosque.

facts.label: caravans
facts.statement: Caravans of merchants crossed the Sahara for safety, and explorers such as Clapperton followed their routes.

facts.label: oases
facts.statement: Oases such as Siwa and Al Kufra dot the Sahara, some fed by wells drilled more than 1,000 feet deep.

facts.label: The Little Prince
facts.statement: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's The Little Prince begins with a pilot crashed in the Sahara.
